explanations: luna: The section's traveler cannot find the road and needs a guide; this prayer asks for الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ, turning that lost-road scene into a direct plea for guidance. | terra: The worshiper directly asks, ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَاطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ, placing the traveler behind the guide and naming the road sought.

luna: The section sets ض ل ل against ه د ي; this verse names the path of those favored and excludes الضَّالِّينَ, giving the road image its clearest guided/lost contrast. | terra: The road is identified as that of recipients of favor and distinguished from the way of those who are lost, joining gift, route, and ضَالِّينَ in one destination.
terra: Those who purchase error in exchange for guidance make a trade that neither profits nor leaves them guided, treating direction as a gift deliberately surrendered.
terra: At humanity's descent to earth, those who follow God's guidance are promised freedom from fear and grief, paralleling the same Adamic road promise in 20:123.

luna: The section defines ض ل ل as missing the way or its destination; ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ states loss of the way's middle, a direct formulation of that image. | terra: Whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, losing precisely the middle of the way that Moses asks to be shown in 28:22.
terra: Wherever people turn, God's face is there; the ayah addresses orientation when no single visible direction can contain the divine presence.
terra: God makes Abraham an imam for people after testing him; leadership is not described as road guidance here, but the appointed person stands before a community as the section's guide does.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss for ء و ي ends a journey at home; this ayah calls the House مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا, a return point and safety, a sacred destination with the shelter's function. | terra: The House is made a place of return and security, so arrival is both repeated homecoming and refuge, the two senses attached to أَوَى in the section.
terra: Abraham asks that the town of the House be secure and its people provided with fruits, extending 2:125's place of return into a safe, provisioned home.
terra: The qiblah objection is answered by saying east and west belong to God and He guides whom He wills to a straight path, joining physical orientation to divine direction.

luna: The section's dictionary form قهقرى means moving backward; this ayah describes turning on one's heels, عَقِبَيْهِ, during the change of prayer direction, a concrete reversal of course after following a direction. | terra: The qiblah distinguishes one who follows the Messenger from one who turns on his heels, while the change is hard except for those God guided; direction, guide, and backward reversal meet.
terra: The Prophet's searching gaze is answered with a commanded direction toward the Sacred Mosque, concretizing the source's example of being unable to find the mosque.

terra: Every community has a direction toward which it turns; the ayah addresses orientation rather than a traveled road, but directly meets the source's secondary image of not knowing which way to seek.
terra: Whenever the Prophet sets out, he is commanded to turn toward the Sacred Mosque, giving departure a fixed destination and bodily direction.

luna: The section says the Prophet was taught what he had not known and then became a guide; this ayah describes the Messenger teaching the Book and wisdom and وَيُعَلِّمُكُم مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ.
luna: The section places a wayfarer beside the orphan and the one who asks; this ayah joins charity to the orphan, needy, petitioner, and ابن السبيل, so the road image meets care for people on it.

terra: The sacrificial offering, هَدْى, is not to be interrupted before it reaches its appointed place; this different branch of the named root still carries an object toward a prescribed destination.

luna: The section links the command to recount God's favor with remembering after guidance; at pilgrimage, this ayah commands remembrance as God هَدَاكُمْ, after the people had earlier been among the lost. | terra: Pilgrims are told to remember God as He guided them, though before that they were among the lost; remembrance becomes the response to having been shown the road.

luna: The section defines هداية as gentle direction; this ayah says there is no compulsion and that الرُّشْد has become distinct from الغَيّ, a specific bridge from showing a clear way to not forcing someone along it.

luna: The section contrasts the unseen night road with visible daylight; this ayah describes God taking believers يُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ, while the opposite movement is assigned to disbelief. | terra: God brings believers out of darknesses into light while false patrons move people the other way, rendering guidance as opposed directions across the night-light boundary.

luna: The section connects عَائِل (poor) with a seeker who does not know which direction to take; this ayah describes needy people unable to make ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ, linking need to blocked travel.

terra: One witness may تَضِلَّ in testimony and be reminded by the other; this may extend the lost-and-guided structure into losing the intended account and being brought back, though no road scene is present.

luna: The section's ه د ي branch B002 gloss says to stay with one's speech or work and not turn away; this prayer asks that hearts not deviate after guidance, a precise boundary against leaving the way. | terra: Those already guided pray that their hearts not deviate afterward; guidance here requires remaining in the received course rather than turning aside.

luna: The section notes that a traveler may lose the mosque or house; this ayah names the House at Bakkah as blessed and هُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ, making a sacred house itself a guidepost. | terra: The first House established for humankind is blessed and a guidance for the worlds; the destination-house itself functions as guidance.
terra: Pilgrimage is owed by whoever is able to find a way to the House, making السَّبِيلِ إِلَيْهِ the concrete route toward the home named in 3:96.
terra: Holding fast to God is described as having been guided to a straight path, giving the source's instruction to stay in one's course a Qur'anic formulation.

luna: The section's note on قهقرى develops a return on one's heels; this ayah asks whether people would turn back on their heels if the Messenger died or were killed. | terra: The possible death of the Messenger prompts the question whether his followers will turn back on their heels, making loss of the leader a test of continued direction.

luna: The section's dictionary form قهقرى means stepping backward; this ayah warns that following disbelievers will turn believers back on their heels, a specific reversal from the guided course. | terra: Believers are warned that obeying rejecters will turn them back on their heels and return them as losers; false leadership reverses their course.
terra: The believers flee uphill without turning toward anyone while the Messenger calls them from behind, a battlefield reversal in which followers run away from their guide's call.

luna: The section ties the Prophet's former lack of knowledge to his later guidance; this ayah describes God's favor in sending a Messenger who recites and teaches the Book and wisdom to people who had been in ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ.

luna: The section's traveler cannot find a way to a destination; these oppressed people are described as unable to devise a plan or find سَبِيلًا out, a specific parallel of being unable to find a route.

luna: This ayah completes 4:98's account of people unable to find a way out by naming the helpless among them and God's pardon; its contribution is the condition that makes their immobility different from chosen straying.

luna: The section says a journey ends in a home and names ء و ي for arriving and settling; this ayah describes emigrants leaving home and finding مَرَاغَمًا and abundance in the earth. | terra: The emigrant leaves home on God's road and will find many places of escape and abundance in the earth; the ayah joins departure, finding, shelter, provision, and even a journey cut short by death.

luna: The section says the Prophet did not know the Book and faith before God guided him; this ayah says God taught him وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُن تَعْلَمُ and gave him the Book and wisdom, naming that gift as God's favor.
terra: A clear proof and manifest light have come from God; 4:175 identifies the straight route and divine destination disclosed by that light.
terra: Those who hold fast to God are admitted to mercy and guided to Him by a straight path; the light announced in 4:174 becomes a route and destination.

terra: Believers may not violate the sacrificial offerings or obstruct visitors heading to the Sacred House for bounty and favor; travelers and the differently sensed هَدْى share the same destination.
terra: After a covenant of worship and support, whoever disbelieves is said to have lost سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, another use of deviation from the road's middle.

luna: The section makes a route visible after darkness; this ayah says نُورٌ وَكِتَابٌ مُّبِينٌ have come, and 5:16 continues by describing guidance to paths of peace, so this row supplies the light that its neighbor turns into a way. | terra: A light and clear Book are said to have come from God; 5:16 states how that light guides seekers through darkness and along paths of peace.

luna: The section moves from a path unseen in darkness to one made visible; this ayah describes being brought out of الظُّلُمَاتِ into النُّور and guided to سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ. | terra: By revelation God guides seekers into paths of peace, brings them from darkness into light, and guides them to a straight path; all three movements of the section converge here.
terra: Moses commands his people to enter the holy land and not turn on their backs or become losers, tying backward retreat to refusal of a named destination.
terra: The holy land is barred and the people wander through the earth for forty years, the direct condition of travelers denied arrival and unable to complete their route.
terra: The sacrificial offering, هَدْيًا, must reach the Kaaba; this different sense of the named ه د ي root still depicts something conducted toward the House as its destination.
terra: At judgment the objects people fabricated vanish from them; what they depended on as a destination or support is itself the thing no longer to be found.
terra: Those who reject the signs are deaf and dumb in darknesses, while God may place a person on a straight path; failed perception and found direction are set against one another.

luna: The section's lost traveler appears here as حَيْرَانَ on earth while companions call him to الهدى; the same ayah asks about turning back on أعقاب after guidance, matching the section's separate dictionary note قهقرى, “to go backward.” | terra: After God has guided them, people are asked whether they should turn back on their heels; the same ayah stages a bewildered man in the land whose companions stand ahead calling him toward guidance.
terra: Night covers Abraham and a star appears, opening the nocturnal search whose failing celestial markers lead to his explicit plea for guidance in 6:77.
terra: When the moon appears and then sets, Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would be among the lost; a night light that fails is set against divine guidance.
terra: The rising sun seems greater but also sets, so even daylight's brightest visible object cannot serve as the ultimate guide sought in the preceding ayah.

luna: The section makes night a time when a traveler cannot see the way; here stars let people يَهْتَدُوا in ظُلُمَاتِ land and sea, a direct nighttime counterpart. | terra: The stars are furnished so travelers may find their way through the darknesses of land and sea; this is the section's invisible night road supplied with guides.

luna: The section's traveler moves from a hidden way at night to a visible route; this ayah compares one given نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ among people with someone in darkness unable to emerge, a direct walking-and-light parallel. | terra: One given light walks among people, unlike one trapped in darkness and unable to emerge; the contrast makes visible what it means for a road to appear after concealment.
terra: God identifies one straight path, commands that it be followed, and forbids the many paths that would split travelers away from it.
terra: Children of Adam are told that messengers will recount God's signs and that those who respond need not fear or grieve, repeating the post-descent provision of guidance through human speakers.
luna: The section links remembrance and speaking of God's favor with having been guided; the people of the Garden say هَدَانَا لِهَذَا, naming their arrival as the result of guidance.
terra: When the promised outcome arrives, fabricated objects of worship vanish from their devotees, reversing the traveler's expectation that the sought object will be waiting.
terra: Those who follow the Messenger also follow the light sent with him; guide, follower, and traveling light form one relation.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to call all people to faith and they are told to follow him so that they may be guided, making the guided messenger a guide for followers.
terra: One whom God leaves astray has no guide, and such people wander blindly in rebellion; the ayah directly combines absent guide, aimless motion, and impaired sight.

luna: The section's verb ء و ي describes being sheltered after vulnerability; this ayah recalls a small, fearful community whom God فَآوَاكُمْ, strengthened, and provided for. | terra: God reminds an endangered, uprooted community that He sheltered them, supported them, and provided good things; آوَاكُمْ repeats the sheltering gift of 93:6 and sets it beside provision.
terra: Satan first presents himself as a protecting companion, then turns back on his heels and disowns his followers; the apparent guide abandons them by the source's backward motion.
terra: Emigrants who leave home are paired with those who shelter and help them, so the journey ends through human hosts enacting the divine shelter named in the source.
terra: A second summary names the believers who migrated and those who sheltered and helped them, confirming that آوَوْا is an enacted response to displacement.
terra: During the migration the Prophet and his companion occupy a cave while God grants tranquility and unseen support; it is a journey interrupted by divinely secured refuge.

luna: The section treats a lost house as a destination someone cannot find; this ayah pictures people seeking any مَلْجَأ, cave, or place of entry to turn into, a concrete image of a refuge sought under pressure.
terra: God does not let a people stray after guiding them until He clarifies what they must avoid, making continued guidance depend on a disclosed boundary.

luna: The section joins a guided road with reaching a home; this ayah says God calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, explicitly pairing destination and route. | terra: God invites to the House of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, joining the route, its guide, and the home in which the journey ends.
terra: Every soul meets what it sent ahead and the invented gods vanish, so arrival discloses that the presumed destination was absent.

luna: The section calls a guide هادٍ because he goes ahead of the traveler; this ayah asks whether the one who يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ is more worthy to be followed than one who needs guidance, making the guide/follower relation explicit. | terra: The ayah asks whether one who guides to truth deserves following more than one unable to guide unless first guided, defining the fitness of the one placed ahead.

luna: The section makes daylight the time a way can be seen; this ayah distinguishes night for rest from النَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا. | terra: God makes night for rest and day sight-giving, giving the source's night and daytime travelers their different fields of visibility.
terra: The Book of Moses is called a leader and mercy before the Quranic witness, making prior revelation an imam that goes before and directs.
terra: Those who lose themselves find their fabrications gone from them; the ayah couples self-loss with loss of the relied-on object.
terra: Noah's son says he will take refuge on a mountain, but the chosen shelter cannot save him; أَوَى is exposed as a false arrival-place.
terra: Under threat, Lot wishes for power or a strong support to which he could take refuge; the longing for shelter is answered by the messengers' night-route command in 11:81.
terra: Lot is told to leave with his family during part of the night and that none should turn back; safe passage depends on obeying the given direction without looking behind.
terra: Pharaoh goes before his people on Judgment Day and brings them to the Fire; the section's defining sign of a guide, preceding followers, is retained while the destination is reversed.
luna: The section's guide precedes the traveler toward a destination; Pharaoh instead يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ toward the Fire, a direct reversal in which leading the way ends at ruin.
luna: The section's ه د ي branch B002 gloss says to remain in the work one is in and not deviate; this command to remain upright, فَاسْتَقِمْ, gives that staying-on-course sense a direct formulation.
terra: A brother predicts that a passing caravan will pick Joseph up from the well, anticipating the traveler who finds the displaced boy in 12:19.
terra: A caravan seeking water finds a boy at the well, so a lost young person is literally found by travelers; the parallel is specific though Joseph's later lodging is supplied in 12:21.
terra: The Egyptian who takes Joseph home tells his wife to make his stay honorable, completing the movement from being found on the road to being lodged in a house.

luna: The section's dictionary form أَوَى describes reaching a home and being sheltered; Yusuf أَوَى his brother to himself in Egypt, a specific arrival and sheltering between kin. | terra: At the end of the brothers' journey Joseph receives his brother to himself, using آوَى for protective family arrival.
terra: Jacob sends his sons to search for Joseph and his brother without despairing; it specifically stages people seeking the lost, but it does not say they are unsure which direction to take.
terra: Joseph receives his parents to himself and tells the family to enter Egypt safely, presenting family reunion as the secure end of a long route.
terra: Every people is said to have a guide; this supports the section's personal guide image, though the ayah does not stage the road itself.
terra: The ayah denies that blindness and sight or darknesses and light are equal, articulating the perceptual boundary presupposed by the hidden and revealed road.

luna: The section's route appears when darkness gives way to daylight; this ayah describes a Book bringing people from الظُّلُمَاتِ to النُّور and guiding them to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy One. | terra: The Book is sent to bring people from darkness into light and onto the path of the Mighty, making revelation the forward guide through an unseen road.

luna: The section recalls Moses finding guidance while traveling; this ayah describes Moses being sent to bring his people مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ, a direct Moses-and-wayfinding parallel. | terra: Moses is told to bring his people from darkness into light; the prophet who was guided on his own journeys now becomes the guide of a people.
terra: The messengers ask why they should not rely on God when He has guided them in their ways, using plural routes for lives that must be patiently continued.
terra: Abraham settles his family by the Sacred House in a barren valley and asks that hearts incline toward them and fruits provide for them, binding destination, dwelling, and provision.
terra: Lot is commanded to travel with his family at night, keep behind them, forbid backward looks, and go exactly where commanded, joining guide position, route, and perseverance.

luna: The section's root note defines the strayer as one who departs from القَصْد; this ayah names قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ and says some of its ways are جَائِرٌ, a close lexical and directional parallel. | terra: The source defines a dāll as one who is جائر عن القصد; this ayah sets قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ against roads that are جَائِرٌ and makes guidance God's act, giving that dictionary line a Qur'anic road.

luna: The section's path becomes visible to a traveler; this ayah places سُبُلًا through the earth so people may تَهْتَدُونَ, making the landscape itself navigable. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and roads are placed on earth so people may find their way; 16:16 then supplies landmarks and stars for the same journey.

luna: The section's nighttime wayfinding is made explicit by landmarks and stars: بِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ says travelers are guided by the star. | terra: Landmarks and stars are means by which people are guided, continuing the physical road scene of 16:15 into night.
luna: The section says the traveler finally reaches and settles in a home; this ayah says God made بُيُوتًا for rest and portable dwellings for travel, joining destination with shelter.
terra: On the day of submission, what people fabricated vanishes from them, making the thing formerly pursued unavailable at arrival.
terra: God chooses Abraham and guides him to a straight path, answering in biographical form the traveler's trust voiced in 37:99.

luna: The section defines هداية as gentle direction; this command tells the Prophet to invite to سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ with wisdom and good counsel, making the manner of guidance concrete. | terra: The command to invite with wisdom and the best manner ends by distinguishing who strays from God's way and who is guided, giving content to guidance as gentle indication.
terra: The servant is carried by night from the Sacred Mosque to the farther mosque and shown signs; this is a complete dark journey between named sacred destinations under divine conduct.
terra: The Quran guides to what is most upright, letting received speech itself perform the directing role that the guided Prophet later performs for others.

luna: The section contrasts night obscurity with the road appearing in daylight; this ayah calls night and day signs, darkens the night sign, and makes the day sign مُبْصِرَةً. | terra: The night sign is erased and the day sign made sight-giving so people may seek bounty; daylight provides the visibility and provision associated with the source's daytime traveler.

luna: The section includes تَنْهَرْ in its source verses for not shouting at the asker; this ayah uses the same root ن ه ر to forbid rebuking one's parents, showing the same prohibition of harsh dismissal in another relation.
luna: The section's traveler may need support on the way; this ayah commands giving the needy and ابن السبيل their due, making the wayfarer's need a social obligation.
terra: One blind here will be blinder in the Hereafter and farther astray from the way, joining failed sight to loss of route.

luna: The section's verb ء و ي concerns finding shelter; these youths أَوَى to a cave and ask their Lord for mercy and a right course, joining shelter to guidance. | terra: The youths take refuge in the cave, أَوَى, and ask their Lord to prepare right guidance for their affair; shelter and guidance are sought together.

luna: The section describes a traveler reaching a place of shelter; these youths are told to take refuge in the cave, فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ, where their Lord will spread mercy for them. | terra: The youths are told to take refuge in the cave, where their Lord will spread mercy and prepare ease; the destination becomes a shelter fitted for them.

terra: The moving sun marks the sheltered cave, then the ayah says the one God guides is guided and the one He leaves astray will find no protecting guide; daylight, refuge, finding, and guidance converge.
terra: After the instruction to remember God when one forgets, the speaker asks to be guided to something nearer to right conduct; recovered memory becomes renewed direction.
terra: For those whose reckoning is deferred, no refuge will ultimately be found apart from God; delayed arrival does not create another home.

luna: The section gives a traveler a sought destination; Moses here resolves to continue until he reaches مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ, a journey organized around reaching a place. | terra: Moses names a destination, the meeting of the two seas, and refuses to cease until he reaches it; this embodies continuing on one's course toward the intended place.

luna: The section distinguishes losing the route from losing the destination; at the meeting of the seas the fish takes its path, سَبِيلَهُ سَرَبًا, and Moses's party loses track of the sign they were following. | terra: At the very junction Moses seeks, the travelers overlook the fish and lose the sign of arrival; the destination is reached before it is recognized.

luna: The section says a traveler may find shelter at a house; the attendant recalls taking refuge at the rock, أَوَيْنَا إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ, while reporting the fish's route into the sea. | terra: The servant recalls that when they took refuge at the rock, أَوَيْنَا, the fish escaped along its way; shelter, a missed sign, and a path meet in one travel scene.

luna: The section's lost destination can be recovered; after recognizing the fish's route as their sign, Moses and his attendant turn back along their tracks, عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا. | terra: Moses recognizes the sought marker and the pair return, retracing their own footprints; backward movement here repairs rather than abandons the route.

luna: After Moses and his attendant retrace their route in 18:64, they find a servant given رَحْمَةً and عِلْمًا; 18:66 identifies him as the person Moses asks to follow, extending the section's traveler-and-guide pairing into a learning journey. | terra: After recovering the place, they find a divinely taught servant; وَجَدَا marks the moment the lost destination yields the guide Moses was seeking.

luna: The section calls a دليل a هادٍ because he goes ahead; Moses asks whether he may أَتَّبِعُكَ, making the guide/follower relation explicit, though the guidance here is knowledge rather than road direction. | terra: Moses asks to follow the servant so that he may teach him right guidance, a literal follower placing himself behind a guide who goes ahead.
terra: Their striving is lost in worldly life while they think they are doing well, so a person can miss the intended line of action without recognizing the deviation.
terra: Abraham tells his father to follow him and promises to guide him onto a level path, the clearest interpersonal staging of the guide walking before another.

luna: In the section's first Moses journey, a fire is seen in the dark and Moses hopes to find guidance there; this ayah puts أَجِدُ and هُدًى together at that fire. | terra: A traveler in darkness sees a distant fire and hopes either for a brand or to find guidance there, joining finding and guidance at the exact point where the night road fails.
terra: When Moses reaches the fire he is called by name, so the night marker sought for road information becomes the place where divine direction is actually encountered.
terra: At the fire Moses learns that he has reached the sacred valley and is told to remove his sandals, confirming arrival at a destination unlike the practical landmark he expected.

luna: The section gives a secondary dictionary sense of هادية as a staff that goes before its holder; this ayah asks Moses what is in his right hand, and 20:18 identifies it as his staff and says he leans on it. The staff matches the object, though this passage does not use it to find a route.

luna: The section names the walking stick الهادية because it goes ahead of its holder; Moses calls his staff عَصَايَ and says he leans on it, أتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا, a concrete traveling use of the same object. | terra: Moses describes the staff in his hand as something he leans upon during ordinary use; it is a concrete traveler's staff, though the ayah does not itself call it the forward-going hādiya of the source dictionary.
terra: The infant Moses is cast into the river, carried to shore, and taken up under God's watch, staging a displaced child whose route to his true caretaker is completed in 20:40.
terra: Moses' sister walks to those who found him and offers to guide them to a caretaker, so guidance returns the displaced child to his mother and a safe home.

luna: The section defines guidance as direction with gentleness and develops Moses's journeys; here God tells Moses and Aaron to speak to Pharaoh with قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا, a specific way of addressing someone toward remembrance. | terra: Moses and Aaron are told to address Pharaoh gently so that he may remember or fear; this is a specific prophetic instance of the source definition of guidance through gentleness, though the ayah does not use هدى.

luna: In Moses's answer to Pharaoh, this ayah says God made the earth a resting place, laid سُبُلًا through it, and sent down rain; the section's traveler gains an earthly route and provision in the same Moses discourse. | terra: The earth is made a cradle and roads are threaded through it, furnishing the physical field on which the section's traveler can move.

luna: The section's traveler cannot manage a night route; Moses is told to travel by night and given طَرِيقًا through the sea, a specific reversal in which a way is made through darkness and danger. | terra: Moses is commanded to lead the servants by night and make a dry road through the sea, with neither fear of being overtaken nor of losing the way.
terra: Pharaoh leads his people astray and does not guide them, naming the failed leader immediately after Moses has opened their night road.
terra: God chooses Adam, turns toward him, and guides him immediately before promising in 20:123 that followers of divine guidance will not lose the way.

luna: The section reverses being lost through guidance; here those who follow God's هُدَى neither يَضِلُّ nor suffer, spelling out what following the guide averts. | terra: After descent to earth, whoever follows God's guidance will neither lose the way nor fall into misery, making faithful following the direct opposite of the source's lost traveler.
terra: Turning away from divine remembrance yields a constricted life and resurrection blind, the perceptual and existential reversal of following guidance in 20:123.

luna: The section's traveler needs a route across the earth; this ayah describes mountain passes made as فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا so people may be guided. | terra: Broad passes are placed through the earth's mountains so people may be guided, making the created road itself an act of guidance.
terra: Prophets are made leaders who guide by God's command, embodying the section's explanation that the guide precedes those being led.
terra: Whoever takes Satan as patron is led astray and guided to the punishment of the Blaze, a false guide carrying a follower to the wrong destination.
terra: God assigns Abraham the site of the House and commands its preparation for those who come to it, a divinely disclosed destination before the travelers are summoned.

luna: The section describes a traveler searching for a mosque or home; this ayah sends pilgrims مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ, on foot and by camel, while 22:26 supplies the House as their destination. | terra: The pilgrimage call brings people on foot and lean mounts from every distant pass, filling the road to the House identified in 22:26.
terra: Mary and her son are sheltered, آوَيْنَاهُمَا, on elevated settled ground with flowing water; refuge is made physically habitable and provisioned.
terra: When God's signs were recited, the hearers recoiled on their heels; revealed speech that should guide instead triggers the source's backward motion.

luna: The section makes guidance bodily visible as a road emerging into daylight; this ayah develops a lamp-and-light image and says يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ, a specific illumination-as-guidance parallel. | terra: The lamp inside layered glass culminates in “light upon light,” and God guides to His light; it supplies a luminous guide rather than leaving the traveler in darkness.
terra: A thirsty traveler reaches what he took for water and finds it nothing, but finds God there; وَجَدَهُ and وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ reverse the expected destination and the act of finding.
terra: Layered darkness at sea leaves a person scarcely able to see even his hand, and without God-given light there is no light; this is the section's inability to pick out a road intensified.
terra: Those who invent comparisons have strayed and cannot find a way, directly joining loss of judgment to inability to locate a route.
luna: The section's guide goes ahead for a traveler to follow; this ayah portrays someone regretting that he did not take سَبِيلًا مَعَ الرَّسُولِ, a concrete failure to follow the guide.

luna: The section's root ض ل ل covers leaving the intended way; this ayah has a speaker say that a companion led him astray from the Reminder after it came, a specific account of a companion diverting someone from guidance.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are worst in place and most astray from the road, reversing upright guided walking and a safe destination.
terra: God makes the sun a guide for the extending shadow; the ayah calls the source of daylight a دَلِيل, the very term the section explains as one who goes ahead.

luna: The section's night walker lacks the day traveler's visibility; this ayah makes night a covering and sleep rest, then describes day as نُشُورًا. | terra: Night is made a covering and day a rising into activity; beside the sun-guide of 25:45, this explains the daily change in the traveler's field of sight.

luna: The section names ض ل ل as missing a way or destination, then cites Moses using الضَّالِّينَ for his earlier state; in Pharaoh's context the word describes his past error, showing the root's nonliteral reach. | terra: Moses names his former condition with ضَالِّينَ; as the section observes, the later speaker and guide first recalls himself as one without the right direction.

luna: The section follows Moses's statement of past ضلال with this next ayah, where he says his Lord granted him حكم; that neighbor supplies the changed condition after the earlier error. | terra: Moses says that after he fled, his Lord granted him judgment and made him a messenger; gift and commissioning answer the former lost state in 26:20.

luna: The section says the nighttime traveler cannot endure night travel; Moses is commanded to take the Israelites out at night, a specific counter-scene of night departure. | terra: God commands Moses to depart with the servants by night because they will be pursued, establishing the dangerous dark journey whose way God then opens.
terra: When the two hosts see one another, Moses' companions believe they have been caught; the apparent end of the road creates the need answered in 26:62-63.

luna: When Moses's people fear they will be overtaken, he says his Lord is with him and سَيَهْدِينِ; this makes the section's Moses-as-lost-traveler motif a crisis of finding a route. | terra: At the blocked sea Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him, locating guidance at the instant no route can yet be seen.

luna: The section's path is a way through terrain; here the sea فَانفَلَقَ for Moses and his people, turning an obstructing landscape into a traversable route. | terra: The sea is split after Moses strikes it, so an impossible boundary becomes the route promised by his words in 26:62.
terra: God saves Moses and all who are with him after the sea opens, supplying the successful arrival-side of the divinely guided route.
terra: Abraham identifies the One who created him as the One who guides him, providing the enduring divine agency behind his later statement that he is going to his Lord.
terra: Moses tells his family that he perceives a fire and may return with news or a burning brand; this repeated scene supplies the family traveler and the distant night marker behind 20:10.
terra: On reaching the fire Moses hears the blessed call, completing the movement from the distant light of 27:7 to the true source of guidance.
terra: The question “Who guides you in the darknesses of land and sea?” makes divine guidance the answer to the traveler's concrete inability to see a route.

luna: The section's traveler cannot see his way in night; this ayah again pairs night rest with النَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا, repeating that perceptual contrast. | terra: Night is made for rest and day for seeing, a repeated formulation of the perceptual difference on which the hidden and visible road depends.
terra: Moses' mother is told to place him in the river without fear and is promised that he will be returned, so a dangerous route begins with assurance of homecoming.
terra: Pharaoh's household picks up the river-borne infant, but the ayah names the future enemy and grief within that apparent shelter; being found does not yet mean reaching the right home.
terra: Pharaoh's wife asks that the found infant not be killed and imagines adopting him, providing a temporary household before he is guided back to his mother.
terra: Moses' sister is told to follow his trace and watches from afar, a literal act of tracking the lost child that enables the guidance offered in 28:12.
terra: Moses' sister asks whether she should guide Pharaoh's household to a family that will care for the infant; the guide leads those holding the found child toward his true household.
terra: Moses is returned to his mother so that she may be comforted, completing the guided movement from loss back into the home.
terra: Moses leaves the city fearful and watchful, asking God for rescue; this supplies the displaced traveler whose request for road guidance follows in 28:22.

luna: The section's second Moses journey is his flight toward Midian; he hopes his Lord will guide him to سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ, explicitly joining travel with the straight-way image. | terra: Moses sets out toward Midian and asks his Lord to guide him to سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, the middle or right line of the road invoked by the source's definition of deviation.
terra: After asking for guidance to the middle of the road, Moses reaches Midian's water; this ayah supplies the first recognized arrival following 28:22.
terra: After reaching Midian and helping the women, Moses withdraws to shade and declares his need for any good God may send, joining arrival with poverty before a home is offered.
terra: A woman comes to Moses, leads him to her father, and the father declares him safe; the guided journey to Midian ends in an offered household and security.

luna: The section recalls Moses finding a fire during travel and seeking guidance; on a later journey this ayah again has Moses see نَارًا, but he seeks news or warmth rather than a path, a close scene with a different need. | terra: Traveling with his family after completing his term, Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring news from it; the ayah makes explicit that the fire appears during a journey whose direction is uncertain.
terra: When Moses reaches the fire, he is called from the side of the valley; the hoped-for wayfinding sign becomes an encounter with the divine speaker.

luna: The section presents the guide as one who leads toward a way; this ayah says Pharaoh's people were made أَئِمَّةً يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ, leaders whose direction is the opposite of guidance. | terra: Leaders are made who call toward the Fire, a direct reversal of leaders who walk ahead toward a safe home.
terra: The Prophet cannot guide everyone he loves, while God guides whom He wills; this sets a boundary around the guided Prophet's guiding role described in 42:52.

terra: When opponents fear that following guidance will uproot them, the reply points to a secure sanctuary to which fruits are brought as provision; guidance, safe home, and enrichment answer their fear together.

luna: The section contrasts travel by day with inability to bear night travel; this ayah assigns night to rest and day to seeking bounty, لِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ, a direct account of stopping and setting out. | terra: Divine mercy appoints night for rest and day for seeking bounty, linking the daylight interval to purposeful movement and provision.
terra: After each community is called for proof, fabricated gods vanish; the failed object of reliance cannot guide or be found when demanded.
terra: The God who imposed the Quran on the Prophet promises to return him to a place of return, turning the prophetic route into an assured homecoming.
terra: A secure sanctuary is contrasted with people being snatched away around it, presenting the sacred home as refuge at the end of surrounding danger.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of ه د ي includes remaining in one's work without departing; this ayah joins striving, جَاهَدُوا, with God's promise to guide people to سُبُلَنَا. | terra: Those who strive toward God are promised guidance in His ways, so sustained movement is answered by routes rather than a single momentary indication.
luna: The section gives night and day different conditions for a traveler; this ayah pairs sleep at night with seeking bounty by day, وَالنَّهَارِ.
luna: The section ties poverty to a lost seeker's uncertainty; this ayah names the relative, needy, and wayfarer as people owed their due, carrying the image of need onto the road.
terra: The Prophet cannot guide the blind out of their wandering; bodily inability to see becomes the boundary image for accepting direction.
terra: The addressee is told to follow the way of one who turns to God and is then reminded of the final return, joining a human route to its destination.
terra: The Book given to Moses is made guidance for the children of Israel, supplying the guidance from which the leaders of 32:24 guide by God's command.
terra: Leaders are appointed to guide by God's command when they remain patient and certain, joining guidance from ahead with perseverance in the course.
terra: The condemned say they obeyed their leaders and great ones, who led them away from the road; following someone ahead does not by itself make that person a true guide.
terra: Visible towns and measured stages let travelers journey safely by nights and days; the route remains legible even at the time the section's traveler cannot endure.
terra: The people ask for greater distances between their stages and are scattered, undoing the visible, measured, safe night-and-day route described in 34:18.
terra: The Prophet says that any straying would fall on himself, whereas his guidance comes through revelation, explicitly locating the source of the guide's own direction.
terra: The blind and the seeing are not equal, introducing the capacity boundary that the darkness-light opposition in 35:20 completes.
terra: Darknesses and light are not equal, the elemental reversal behind whether the traveler can discern a way.
terra: Barriers are set before and behind people and their sight is covered, so neither the road ahead nor retreat can be seen.
terra: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city and tells his people to follow the messengers; he physically arrives to point them toward the guided leaders named in 36:21.
terra: People are told to follow messengers who ask no payment and are themselves guided; the one ahead is fit to guide because he has first received guidance.
terra: Worship of God is named “a straight path” between the prohibition on following Satan and the reminder that Satan led many astray.
terra: If sight were effaced, people would race toward the path but could not see it; the ayah directly separates having a road from being able to discern it.
terra: If fixed or transformed in place, people could neither proceed nor return, setting forward travel and backward movement at the boundary of bodily ability.
terra: The command “guide them to the path of Hell” preserves guide, path, and destination but makes every element carry the opposite end.

luna: The section pairs travel with hope that God will guide the traveler; Abraham says he is going to his Lord and that He will guide him, سَيَهْدِينِ. | terra: Abraham announces that he is going to his Lord and that his Lord will guide him, stating movement, destination, and guide in one first-person journey.
terra: The disputants ask David to guide them to the even road, سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ; judicial direction is expressed through the same middle-of-the-way image.
terra: Those who listen to speech and follow its best meaning are the ones God has guided, joining received words, following, and guidance.
terra: One whose breast God opens is upon a light from his Lord; the ayah locates a guided person in illumination even though it does not describe literal travel.
terra: The ayah states that one God leaves astray has no guide, isolating the absence of the forward guide as the decisive condition.
terra: No one can lead astray the person God guides, completing 39:36's two-sided boundary between direction and loss.
terra: Pharaoh claims that he guides his people only to the way of right conduct; 40:38 exposes the rival claim by offering a guide whose destination is salvation.
terra: The warned day is described as a day of turning one's backs, when no protector can save and no guide exists for one God leaves astray.
terra: The believing man tells his people to follow him and promises to guide them to the way of right direction, standing before them against Pharaoh's rival claim.

luna: The section's night is difficult for a traveler and daylight opens the way; this ayah repeats night for rest and النَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا. | terra: God makes night for rest and day sight-giving, repeating the concrete day-night boundary behind the traveler's ability to choose a road.
terra: People confess that those they invoked have vanished from them, an after-arrival recognition that the sought supports were never a true destination.
terra: Thamud prefer blindness to guidance, choosing precisely the perceptual state in which the section's road disappears.
terra: Former objects of prayer vanish and their worshipers know there is no escape, pairing a lost false destination with the absence of a route away.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to call, remain straight as ordered, and not follow desires; this closely matches the source gloss “continue in your speech or work and do not turn from it.”
terra: Those left astray have no protector and ask whether there is any road back, making lost guidance inseparable from an unavailable return route.
terra: Before the unavoidable day arrives, people are told they will have no refuge and no power to deny their deeds, marking the final boundary on seeking another shelter.

luna: The section says the one who was guided becomes a guide; this ayah addresses the Prophet, says he had not known the Book or faith, then says he guides to a straight path, making that change explicit. | terra: The Prophet once did not know Book or faith, but the revealed light now lets him guide to a straight path; the guided one has become the guide.

luna: The section's road is a route across the earth; this ayah says God made سُبُلًا in the earth so people may find guidance, closely joining path and هداية. | terra: God makes the earth a resting place and places roads in it so people may be guided, joining habitable ground with traversable direction.
terra: Devilish companions bar people from the path while those people suppose themselves guided, showing that confidence in direction can coexist with actual loss.
terra: The Prophet is told to hold fast to what was revealed because he is on a straight path, matching the source's instruction to keep to one's current word or work without veering.
terra: Moses is again commanded to take God's servants away by night because they will be pursued, a repeated dark-road scene whose opened path is explicit elsewhere.
terra: A seal over hearing and heart and a covering over sight end in the question who can guide after God; obscured perception marks the boundary of finding the way.
terra: The Book of Moses is described as a leader and mercy, while the confirming Arabic Book warns and gives good news; “leader” gives revelation the forward position of a guide.
terra: The supposed gods fail to help and vanish because they were fabricated, showing false guides and destinations disappearing at the point of need.
terra: The jinn describe the Book after Moses as guiding to truth and to a straight road; transmitted speech takes the guide's place before hearers who can follow.
terra: Those already guided receive increased guidance, showing that direction is sustained and augmented after entry onto the way.

luna: The section's backward-step dictionary sense illuminates this ayah's people who turn back after guidance has become clear; it is a direct reversal of remaining on the shown way. | terra: People turn back after guidance has become clear, so the section's rearward movement becomes deliberate abandonment of a disclosed route.
terra: God promises to guide the same prophetic addressee to a straight path, a direct counterpart to the remembered favor in 93:7.
terra: The sacrificial offerings, ٱلْهَدْىَ, are prevented from reaching their appointed place; a different sense of the guidance root is bound to a journey blocked short of its destination.
terra: The Prophet's companion is declared neither to have strayed nor erred; this protects his revelatory stance while 93:7 can still recall a prior need for divine direction.
terra: Clear signs are sent down to bring people from darkness into light, repeating the movement from a concealed world into one in which a way can be seen.

luna: The section calls a guide هادٍ because he precedes the traveler; on the Day of Judgment this ayah puts believers' light, نُورُهُم بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ, before them as they are given news of the Garden, a specific light-leading-to-destination image. | terra: The believers' light runs before them as they approach the gardens, a visible realization of the guide who advances ahead of the traveler toward the final dwelling.
terra: Hypocrites ask to borrow the believers' forward-running light and are told to turn back to seek light, after which a barrier divides the two groups.

luna: The section ties guidance to a path made visible; this ayah promises believers a light by which they walk, نُورًا تَمْشُونَ بِهِ, making illumination usable as a guide. | terra: God promises believers a light by which they walk, turning guidance in darkness into a carried means of travel.

luna: The section's traveler may lose a home and need shelter; this ayah describes poor emigrants أُخْرِجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِمْ and wealth who seek God's favor and support, making displacement and need concrete.

luna: The section connects arrival at shelter with being provided for; this ayah describes the people of Medina who تَبَوَّءُوا الدَّارَ welcoming emigrants into their homes and preferring them despite their own need.
terra: After Moses' people deviate, God causes their hearts to deviate; the ayah makes turning from the received line the opposite of staying in one's guidance.

luna: The section says the Prophet lacked knowledge of the Book and faith before being made a guide; this ayah says a Messenger teaches the Book and wisdom to a people formerly in ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ, joining teaching with release from error.
terra: The believers' light runs before them and they ask God to perfect it, repeating the image of illumination advancing ahead of travelers toward their promised destination.
terra: Pharaoh's wife asks God to build her a house near Him in the Garden and save her from Pharaoh; it gives the threatened person a true final home, though no guiding journey is narrated.
luna: The section places a traveler on a route and recalls provision; this ayah calls the earth manageable, tells people to walk its مَنَاكِبِ, and joins that movement to eating God's provision.
terra: The ayah asks whether one who walks fallen on his face is better guided than one walking upright on a straight path, giving guidance a bodily posture and traversable line.
terra: A visitation reaches the garden by night while its owners sleep, so the change in their destination occurs while darkness hides it.
terra: By morning the garden has become like a stripped or darkened field; dawn reveals that the travelers' intended place is no longer what they expected.
terra: At daybreak the owners call one another to set out, supplying the morning departure that leads to their mistaken declaration of being lost.
terra: They urge one another to go early to their crop, naming the destination and purpose of the dawn journey.
terra: On seeing the altered garden they say إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ, first construing the lost destination as having taken the wrong way.
terra: They correct themselves: they are not merely lost but deprived, مَحْرُومُونَ; the correction meets the section's link between directional loss and need.
terra: God makes the earth an expanse, supplying the traversable ground on which the broad roads of 71:20 run.

luna: The section's image is a path that can be walked; this ayah describes فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا in the earth so people may pass through them. | terra: The earth is spread so people may traverse its broad roads; it supplies the physical road-field, although no lost traveler or guide is named.
terra: The heard recitation guides to right conduct, so the revealed word itself becomes the guide encountered by its listeners.
terra: The Prophet says he would find neither protector nor refuge apart from God; the negative وَأَجِدَ ... مُلْتَحَدًا marks the boundary beyond which no shelter can be reached.
terra: On that day the human being is told there is no place of escape, closing every imagined route away before 75:12 names the true destination.
terra: After every escape is denied in 75:11, this ayah names the final destination as being to the Lord, completing the journey boundary.
terra: God says He showed the human being the way, leaving gratitude or ingratitude as the response after direction has been supplied.

luna: The section's poor person and vulnerable petitioner are people encountered along a journey; this ayah describes feeding the needy, orphan, and captive, turning vulnerability into a reason to give.

luna: The section's nighttime way is hidden from the traveler; this ayah calls the night لِبَاسًا, a covering, giving the dark side of the section's day/night contrast. | terra: Night is made a covering, the concealment that explains why the traveler cannot discern the route before 78:11's active day.

luna: The section labels ن ه ر (B002) as the root behind the daytime traveler; this ayah says the day, النَّهَارَ, was made مَعَاشًا, the moving and working side of the contrast. | terra: Day is made the time of livelihood, fitting the source's “daytime man” who moves and seeks provision once concealment lifts.

luna: The section says the road appears at ضحى after the dark night; this ayah pairs the night it darkens with its ضُحَاهَا, the brightness brought out after it. | terra: God darkens the night and brings out its morning brightness, ضُحَىٰهَا; the same named root marks the transition by which a hidden road can appear.

luna: The section's root note says a road دَحَا when it appeared; this ayah uses دَحَاهَا for spreading the earth after 79:29 describes night darkening and daylight emerging. The sense differs, so this is only a tentative reminder of the ground on which a revealed route lies.
terra: The question “Where, then, are you going?” exposes uncertainty about direction before 81:28 names the possibility of taking a straight course.
terra: The reminder is for whoever wills to go straight, giving the bewildered addressee of 81:26 a course to choose and remain upon.
luna: The section prohibits overpowering an orphan; this ayah rebukes those who do not honor the orphan, a concrete contrary treatment of the same person.
luna: The section's poor and asking figure call for response; this ayah rebukes failure to urge feeding the needy, a specific reversal of answering need.

luna: The section describes a traveler who loses his intended direction; this ayah says the human being was shown النَّجْدَيْنِ, making the image a choice between routes. | terra: God says He guided the human being to the two ascending ways, presenting guidance as disclosure of divergent roads that demand a choice.
luna: The section develops the road as a route one may or may not find; this ayah says the person did not attempt الْعَقَبَةَ, a road left untaken before the acts of care that explain it.
luna: This ayah asks what الْعَقَبَةُ is, opening the explanation in 90:13, 90:14, 90:15, and 90:16; it makes the path image a moral difficulty rather than a geographic route.
luna: The section pairs finding a way with treatment of vulnerable people; this ayah names فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ as the first act on the steep ascent, turning a hard path into a course of care.
luna: The section connects wayfinding with its later appeal to care for the poor; this ayah begins the difficult ascent by feeding during ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ, a day of hunger, linking a hard way with aid.
luna: The section includes the orphan under the prohibition against overpowering; this ayah places يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ, an orphan of close kin, in the hard ascent's scene of feeding.
luna: The section joins a traveler's poverty to uncertainty about direction; this ayah adds مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ, a needy person in the dust, to the ascent, making need visible as hardship.
luna: After 90:13 names freeing a person, 90:14 feeding the hungry, 90:15 the orphan, and 90:16 the destitute, this ayah adds وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ; it makes the path a shared moral course.
luna: This ayah calls those who take the steep ascent أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ; it completes 90:11's path of care with the group that succeeds in it, echoing the section's road toward a good end.

luna: The section names root ض ح و for ضُحَى, the hour when a road appears; this oath names the sun and its ضُحَاهَا, anchoring the image's daylight term in the sun's brightness. | terra: The sun is sworn by together with its morning brightness, ضُحَىٰهَا, naming the light source whose revealing action 91:3 sets against night.

luna: The section says a road appears at ضُحَى; this oath names the day when it جَلَّاهَا, making day the time when what was hidden is brought to view. | terra: Day is sworn by when it discloses or displays the sun, echoing the source's road that becomes visible in daylight.
terra: Night is sworn by when it covers the sun, reversing 91:3's disclosure and supplying the concealment in which the road disappears.

luna: The section's night traveler cannot see the road; this oath names the night as it يَغْشَى, covering what is there. | terra: The night is sworn by as it covers, supplying the concealing half of the road image that 92:2 reverses.

luna: The section says the road appears when daylight comes; this oath names the day as it تَجَلَّى, the counterpart to the night that covers in 92:1. | terra: The day is sworn by as it becomes manifest, directly reversing the night's covering and echoing the source gloss in which the road “becomes apparent.”
terra: Within the same night-and-day surah, God declares that guidance belongs to Him, placing the giver of direction behind the alternation of concealment and disclosure.
terra: Quraysh's winter and summer journeys place repeated travel behind the commands about the House, food, and security in the next two ayat.
terra: The travelers are told to worship the Lord of this House, making the home at the center of their journeys the focus of response.
terra: The Lord of the House feeds against hunger and grants safety from fear, placing provision and security at the journey's settled center.
luna: The section's 93:9 forbids overpowering the orphan; this ayah depicts the contrary act of repelling him, a direct reversal of the section's injunction.
luna: The section's image includes poverty and prohibits driving away the asker; this ayah condemns failing to urge the feeding of the needy, reversing care for the vulnerable.
